title: Credit analysis software: what it automates, and 9 tools compared for 2026
summary: Credit analysis software compared for community banks and credit unions: nine tools on spreading, DSCR, policy checks, the credit memo and LOS fit.

What is credit analysis software?


Credit analysis software works out whether a business borrower can repay a loan. It spreads the borrower’s statements and tax returns into one standard grid, computes ratios such as debt service coverage, tests the file against the lender’s credit policy and drafts the credit memo a committee reads. A person still makes the decision.


Quick answer


Kita is the best credit analysis software for community banks and credit unions in 2026. It spreads the financials with every figure cited, computes DSCR, flags risk the ratios miss, checks your credit policy and drafts a cited credit memo, on every loan type. Abrigo, nCino, Moody’s, Baker Hill and MeridianLink build it into lending systems, Aloan serves bank commercial desks, Kaaj serves small business and equipment finance lenders, and Uptiq works beside your LOS. Kita is our product.


Key takeaways


Kita has a check in every scorecard column. It spreads the file, computes the ratios, flags what they miss, applies your credit policy and drafts the memo.


Kita fits either way: it integrates with any LOS, core, CRM, bureau, data provider, servicing or e-sign tool, or runs end to end as Intelligent LOS.


Test with your own files: a photographed statement, a return with K-1s, a known altered document and a file that breaks your policy.


**Best overall:** Kita, with your underwriter deciding. Ask every vendor for a quote at your volume.


Picture a made-up family bakery with two shops that wants a loan for a third oven line. It sends the last three years of tax returns, a year-end profit and loss statement and a phone photo of a bank statement. Before a community bank or credit union can say yes, someone has to ask whether the bakery earns enough to repay, and what the numbers do not show.


That work is credit analysis. An analyst retypes the figures into one grid, called spreading, so each year sits beside the last. They then compute ratios such as debt service coverage: the cash a business makes divided by the loan payments it owes, where 1.25 means a quarter more cash than the debt needs.


They test the result against the credit policy, the lender’s written rules, and write the credit memo, the case that a credit committee reads before it approves. Credit analysis software does that work and leaves the decision to a person.


For the spreading step alone, read[our comparison of financial spreading software](https://www.kita.ai/blog/best-financial-spreading-software) .


### Credit analysis is five jobs, in order


Credit analysis software earns its name by how many of these it does. The decision stays with your underwriter.


1. 01


Spread


Restate the returns and statements in one grid, period by period, so years can be compared.


2. 02


Compute the ratios


Work out measures such as debt service coverage: cash the business makes divided by the loan payments it owes.


3. 03


Look past the ratios


Spot what numbers alone hide: one customer paying most of the bills, margins sliding, a late filing.


4. 04


Test against policy


Check the file against the lender’s written credit policy and list every exception.


5. 05


Write the memo, then decide


Turn the analysis into the credit memo a committee reads. A person reads it and makes the call.


A simplification, not a claim about any one product. Kita does the first four jobs and drafts the memo that the lender's underwriter reads before deciding.


This guide compares nine tools and ranks Kita first. Each competitor entry uses only what the vendor publishes on its own site, cited in the references and fetched on November 21, 2026. Speed and delivery figures are the vendors’ own, and we did not test them. This guide is written by a vendor, and says so: Kita is our product.


## What does credit analysis software actually do?


It does five jobs in order. It reads the documents and builds the spread. It computes the ratios, including DSCR. It looks for risk the numbers hide, such as one customer paying most of the bills or margins sliding for three periods. It tests the file against the credit policy and flags every exception. It then drafts the credit memo from the numbers and the exceptions, so the committee has something to read.


What it leaves to people is judgment: whether an owner’s loan counts as debt, how much a falling margin matters and whether an exception is worth making. Kita does the five jobs on one file and hands the underwriter a memo that is already written, with every figure cited to its source line.\[1,2\] Our[credit analysis software](https://www.kita.ai/credit-analysis-software) page shows the signals Kita reads beyond the ratios, and the[AI Underwriter](https://www.kita.ai/ai-underwriter) page shows how a file moves through it.


## How is credit analysis different from spreading, underwriting and a loan origination system?


The terms overlap, and vendors use them loosely. Spreading is the first step: turning documents into a standard grid. Credit analysis is spreading plus the ratios, the risk reading, the policy test and the memo. Underwriting is the wider process, which also covers collecting the file from the borrower and the decision. A loan origination system, or LOS, is the system that tracks the application from start to booking.


Some tools sell only the analysis, some bundle it inside an LOS, and some do the whole path. Kita covers the analysis end to end and also the rest of the file, so it works whichever way you buy. See our[loan underwriting software](https://www.kita.ai/loan-underwriting-software) page for the loan types it handles, and our[comparison of commercial loan underwriting software](https://www.kita.ai/blog/best-commercial-loan-underwriting-software) for the wider process.


## What kinds of credit analysis software are there?


The tools sold under this name differ most in where the analysis lives. Some come as a module of a lending system, some work on the borrower’s documents and pass the result to the system you run, and one builds the origination system around the analysis.

## How do you choose credit analysis software for a community bank or credit union?


Six questions separate these tools more than any feature list.


-


**Does it build the spread, or wait for you to?** Kita turns statements, tax returns, K-1s and bank data into a normalized period-over-period spread without rekeying.\[1,6,7\] Aloan says financial data is spread into the institution’s format, and Uptiq reads 1040, 1120, 1120-S and 1065 returns and K-1s.\[16,20\]


-


**Can it trace every figure?** Kita’s memo cites every claim to its source line, so an analyst or an examiner can check any number against the document that produced it.\[1\] Aloan says every number maps back to the exact source page, and Uptiq puts a citation behind every number.\[16,20\]


-


**Does it compute the ratios and read past them?** Kita computes DSCR, margin, debt service and trend in one pass, then flags concentration risk, moving margins and what a late filing implies.\[1,2\] Aloan says it calculates DSCR, leverage and liquidity and flags revenue declines and concentration risks, and Kaaj says it provides DSCR, leverage, profitability and cash flow views.\[16,18\]


-


**Does it apply your policy, and flag what breaks it?** Kita holds every file against your encoded credit policy and flags anything outside it.\[1,2\] Aloan says it identifies specific exceptions with supporting evidence, and Uptiq says it applies the institution’s DSCR thresholds and leverage limits.\[16,20\]


-


**Does it check the document before it trusts it?** An analysis built on an edited statement is a faster route to the wrong answer. Kita Capture checks for tampering and metadata edits.\[5\] Kaaj says it checks every document against 25+ forensic signals at intake, and Aloan says its fraud detection covers document authenticity.\[19,16\]


-


**Does it fit your stack?** Kita integrates with any LOS or runs as Intelligent LOS, so the choice stays yours.\[1,8\] Abrigo, nCino, Moody’s, Baker Hill and MeridianLink offer analysis inside their own lending systems, so using it means adopting the system.\[10,11,13,14,15\]


Our recommendation is Kita: it answers yes to all six and covers the whole analysis, then hands the booked loan to any servicing system. If you only need part of the job, the lending systems bring analysis with their own system, and Aloan, Kaaj and Uptiq work on the file beside your LOS.


For a community institution the examiner is the other reader. Kita keeps every figure linked to the document line that produced it, records every policy check and has a named person sign the decision, and Kita is SOC 2 Type II compliant and ISO 27001 certified.\[2,9\]


## How do you test credit analysis software on your own files?


A demo on a clean sample proves little. Run the same six-step test on every tool on your shortlist.


-


**Pick five closed files** from the last year, with the spreads and memos your analysts wrote.


-


**Make one messy:** a photographed statement, a scan with a missing page or a non-standard layout.


-


**Include a return with K-1s** and check that the ownership schedules land in the right rows.


-


**Add one known altered document** and see whether the tool catches it before it builds on the numbers.


-


**Include a file that breaks your policy** and see whether the tool names the rule it breaks.


-


**Compare the totals, ratios and memo** with your analysts’ work, and time each file from upload to a memo an underwriter can review.

## Frequently asked questions


### What is the best credit analysis software for community banks and credit unions?


Kita is the best credit analysis software for most community banks and credit unions because it does the whole analysis in one platform: it spreads tax returns and statements into a normalized grid, computes DSCR and the other ratios, flags risk the ratios miss, holds the file against your credit policy and drafts a credit memo with every claim cited to its source line, on every loan type. Abrigo, nCino, Moody’s CreditLens, Baker Hill and MeridianLink offer analysis inside a lending system, Aloan is built for bank commercial desks, Kaaj is focused on small business, equipment finance and MCA lenders, and Uptiq works beside your LOS. Run one of your closed files through Kita to see the result.


### What is credit analysis software, and how does it work?


Credit analysis software works out whether a business borrower can repay a loan. It spreads the borrower’s financial statements and tax returns into one standard grid, computes ratios such as debt service coverage, tests the file against the lender’s credit policy and drafts the credit memo that a credit committee reads. It does not make the lending decision. The lender’s underwriter reads the memo and decides, and the better tools show the source of every figure so that the reading is quick.


### What is AI credit analysis, and does the AI make the credit decision?


AI credit analysis uses AI to do the analyst’s file work: reading documents, building the spread, computing ratios, checking policy and drafting the memo. The decision stays with a person. Kita drafts and explains, with every figure cited to its source, and the lender’s underwriter makes every decision.


### Do we have to replace our loan origination system to get better credit analysis?


No. Kita integrates with any external system, including any LOS, core, CRM, credit bureau, data provider, servicing or e-sign tool, and lenders that want one origination system can run the whole process in Kita’s Intelligent LOS. Kaaj and Uptiq say they work beside an existing LOS, Aloan says it can run as the LOS or alongside one, and Abrigo, nCino, Moody’s, Baker Hill and MeridianLink offer analysis as part of their own lending systems.


### How long does it take to implement credit analysis software?


Kita is set up with your own credit policy in under 24 hours, and later changes ship just as fast. Uptiq says most commercial banks are live in 5 business days, Aloan says most lenders are live within 2 to 4 weeks, Kaaj says two to three weeks after a pilot on your own deals, and MeridianLink’s launch post says 90 days or less. Whichever you choose, ask each vendor what the calendar depends on.

Its AI Credit Officer collects documents from borrowers, Kita Capture reads and checks them, and its AI Underwriter spreads the financials, computes DSCR, margin and trend, holds the file against the lender’s own credit policy and drafts a credit assessment with every figure cited to its source line.
